summary: Stephen G. Covell works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Princeton University (~1995–2001) under Jacqueline I. Stone and took a post at Western Michigan University around 2001.

Stephen G. Williams works in philosophy. He studied at the University of Oxford and at Colorado State University (~2016–2018), where Matthew MacKenzie served on his committee, and held a post at Worcester College.

Stephen H. West is a sinologist who studied at National Taiwan Normal University and the University of Michigan (~1964–1972). He held professorships at the University of Arizona (~1972–1986), UC Berkeley (~1986–2002), and Arizona State University (~2002).

Stephen J. Laumakis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, and George J. Tanabe, Jr. In 1990, he became Professor of Philosophy and Honors Program Director at the University of St. Thomas.

Stephen L. Jenkins was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Harvard (~-1999) under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey. He worked at Taisho University and was Professor of Religious Studies at Cal Poly Humboldt (~2000–2016).

Stephen Prothero is a religious studies scholar. He studied at Yale University and Jonathan Edwards College (~1978–1982) and Harvard University (~1986–1990), later taking a post at Boston University around 1996.

Stephen R. Bokenkamp is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied at UC Berkeley (~1974–1986). He held posts at Indiana University (~1989–2007), the Australian National University (1999), and Arizona State University (~2007).
Stephen Suen is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong (~2005–2009) under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Steve Odin works in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Stony Brook University (~1976–1980) under David A. Dilworth, Edward S. Casey, and Sung Bae Park, and held posts at Stony Brook, the University of Hawaii (1982), and elsewhere.
Steve Schmidt is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under traditional teachers Buddhadasa Bhikkhu and Ajahn Poh.

Steven Collins specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich, and held posts at Exeter College, Oxford, the University of Bristol (~1980–1991), and the University of Chicago (1991).

Steven Edward Lindquist specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (~1999–2005) under Patrick Olivelle, and held a post at Concordia University (~2005–2006).

Steven Heine works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1968–1972) and Temple University (~1973–1980), later holding posts at Penn State (1992–1993) and Florida International University (~1997).

Steven Lukes works in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Balliol College and Nuffield College, Oxford, and held posts at Worcester College, Keele University, Balliol College (~1966–1987), EUI, Siena, LSE, and NYU (~2001).

Steven Neal Weinberger specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College and the University of Virginia, completing his doctorate under Jeffrey Hopkins by 2003, and subsequently held a post at the University of Virginia.
Steven Smith is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under teachers U Pandita and Anagarika Munindra.

Sthaneshwar Timalsina works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~2001–2005), he held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, San Diego State University (~2005–2021), and Stony Brook University (~2021).

Stig Wikander was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala and Copenhagen under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, Arthur Christensen, and Geo Widengren, later holding posts at Lund (1941–1953) and Uppsala (1953–1974).
Stuart Ray Sarbacker works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1995–2001) under doctoral supervisor David M. Knipe.
Su Bai was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Peking University (~1944–1948) and later served there as a professor (~1950–2004).
